title: Finite chain countermodels and decidability for Dummett logic

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic, Winter 2019/20 (notes dated January 2, 2020)
based_on.pages: §1.8 and §2, printed pp.25–29; finite geometric tracing developed locally

based_on.title: Filtration (March 14, 2012)

summary: Preserve rooted comparability through finite filtration, then add a chain test to the finite-code search for Dummett consequence.
abstract: A finite model with a greatest world can still branch into incomparable alternatives, and such a diamond refutes Dummett linearity. Finite countermodels for Dummett logic must instead be chains. We begin with its rooted canonical countermodel and show that finite forcing traces retain comparisons as well as the required premise truths and conclusion failure. The resulting chain fits the same subformula bound used for weak excluded middle. Adding an explicit comparison test to the existing finite-table search therefore decides finite Dummett consequence. The two-world excluded-middle countermodel survives this extra test, while the diamond does not, showing where the two intermediate logics differ.
